Apply properties of operations to calculate with numbers in any form; convert between forms as appropriate; and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies. For example: If a woman making $25 an hour gets a 10% raise, she will make an additional 1/10 of her salary an hour, or $2.50, for a new salary of $27.50. If you want to place a towel bar 9 3/4 inches long in the center of a door that is 27 1/2 inches wide, you will need to place the bar about 9 inches from each edge; this estimate can be used as a check on the exact computation.

domain: Expressions and Equations (7.EE)
skill: Construct equations/inequalities to solve problems
description: Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or mathematical problem, and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.

domain: Expressions and Equations (7.EE)
skill: Solve word problems as px + q = r equations
description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently. Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach. For example, the perimeter of a rectangle is 54 cm. Its length is 6 cm. What is its width?

domain: Expressions and Equations (7.EE)
skill: Solve word problems as inequalities and graph solutions
description: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem. For example: As a salesperson, you are paid $50 per week plus $3 per sale. This week you want your pay to be at least $100. Write an inequality for the number of sales you need to make, and describe the solutions.

domain: Geometry (7.G)
skill: Solve problems involving scale drawings
description: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, including computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.

domain: Geometry (7.G)
skill: Draw geometric shapes with given conditions
description: Draw (freehand, with ruler and protractor, and with technology) geometric shapes with given conditions. Focus on constructing triangles from three measures of angles or sides, noticing when the conditions determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle.

domain: Geometry (7.G)
skill: Describe 2D figures from slicing 3D figures
description: Describe the two-dimensional figures that result from slicing three-dimensional figures, as in plane sections of right rectangular prisms and right rectangular pyramids.

domain: Geometry (7.G)
skill: Know and use circle area/circumference formulas
description: Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems; give an informal derivation of the relationship between the circumference and area of a circle.

domain: Geometry (7.G)
skill: Use facts about angle relationships to solve for unknowns
description: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write and solve simple equations for an unknown angle in a figure.

domain: Geometry (7.G)
skill: Solve area, volume, surface area problems
description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume and surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms.

domain: Statistics and Probability (7.SP)
skill: Understand random sampling and representativeness
description: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population; generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. Understand that random sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid inferences.

domain: Statistics and Probability (7.SP)
skill: Draw inferences from random sample data
description: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions. For example, estimate the mean word length in a book by randomly sampling words from the book; predict the winner of a school election based on randomly sampled survey data. Gauge how far off the estimate or prediction might be.

domain: Statistics and Probability (7.SP)
skill: Assess visual overlap of two data distributions
description: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability. For example, the mean height of players on the basketball team is 10 cm greater than the mean height of players on the soccer team, about twice the variability (mean absolute deviation) on either team; on a dot plot, the separation between the two distributions of heights is noticeable.

domain: Statistics and Probability (7.SP)
skill: Draw comparative inferences using center/variability
description: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations. For example, decide whether the words in a chapter of a seventh-grade science book are generally longer than the words in a chapter of a fourth-grade science book.

domain: Statistics and Probability (7.SP)
skill: Understand probability as a number between 0 and 1
description: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around 1/2 indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.

domain: Statistics and Probability (7.SP)
skill: Approximate probability from observed frequency
description: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability. For example, when rolling a number cube 600 times, predict that a 3 or 6 would be rolled roughly 200 times, but probably not exactly 200 times.

domain: Statistics and Probability (7.SP)
skill: Develop and use a probability model
description: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events. Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.

domain: Statistics and Probability (7.SP)
skill: Develop a uniform probability model
description: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events. For example, if a student is selected at random from a class, find the probability that Jane will be selected and the probability that a girl will be selected.

domain: Statistics and Probability (7.SP)
skill: Develop a probability model from observed frequencies
description: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process. For example, find the approximate probability that a spinning penny will land heads up or that a tossed paper cup will land open-end down. Do the outcomes for the spinning penny appear to be equally likely based on the observed frequencies?

domain: Statistics and Probability (7.SP)
skill: Find probabilities of compound events
description: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.

domain: Statistics and Probability (7.SP)
skill: Understand compound event probability as fraction of outcomes
description: Understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.

domain: Statistics and Probability (7.SP)
skill: Represent sample spaces for compound events
description: Represent sample spaces for compound events using methods such as organized lists, tables and tree diagrams. For an event described in everyday language (e.g., “rolling double sixes”), identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event.

domain: Statistics and Probability (7.SP)
skill: Design and use a simulation for compound events
description: Design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events. For example, use random digits as a simulation tool to approximate the answer to the question: If 40% of donors have type A blood, what is the probability that it will take at least 4 donors to find one with type A blood?

domain: The Number System (8.NS)
skill: Know that irrational numbers have non-repeating decimals
description: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational. Understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion; for rational numbers show that the decimal expansion repeats eventually, and convert a decimal expansion which repeats eventually into a rational number.

domain: The Number System (8.NS)
skill: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers
description: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on a number line diagram, and estimate the value of expressions (e.g., π²). For example, by truncating the decimal expansion of √2, show that √2 is between 1 and 2, then between 1.4 and 1.5, and explain how to continue on to get better approximations.

domain: Expressions and Equations (8.EE)
skill: Apply properties of integer exponents
description: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions. For example, 3² × 3⁻⁵ = 3⁻³ = 1/3³ = 1/27.

domain: Expressions and Equations (8.EE)
skill: Use square/cube root symbols to solve equations
description: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³ = p, where p is a positive rational number. Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect cubes. Know that √2 is irrational.

domain: Expressions and Equations (8.EE)
skill: Estimate quantities using powers of 10
description: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities, and to express how many times as much one is than the other. For example, estimate the population of the United States as 3 × 10⁸ and the population of the world as 7 × 10⁹, and determine that the world population is more than 20 times larger.

domain: Expressions and Equations (8.EE)
skill: Perform operations in scientific notation
description: Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation, including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities (e.g., use millimeters per year for seafloor spreading). Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology.

domain: Expressions and Equations (8.EE)
skill: Graph proportional relationships and compare rates
description: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways. For example, compare a distance-time graph to a distance-time equation to determine which of two moving objects has greater speed.

domain: Expressions and Equations (8.EE)
skill: Use similar triangles to derive linear equations
description: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; derive the equation y = mx for a line through the origin and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b.

domain: Expressions and Equations (8.EE)
skill: Solve linear equations in one variable
description: Solve linear equations in one variable.

domain: Expressions and Equations (8.EE)
skill: Give examples of linear equations with varied solution sets
description: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the case by successively transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an equivalent equation of the form x = a, a = a, or a = b results (where a and b are different numbers).

domain: Expressions and Equations (8.EE)
skill: Solve linear equations with rational coefficients
description: Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients, including equations whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and collecting like terms.

domain: Expressions and Equations (8.EE)
skill: Analyze and solve simultaneous linear equations
description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

domain: Expressions and Equations (8.EE)
skill: Understand solutions as points of intersection
description: Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

domain: Expressions and Equations (8.EE)
skill: Solve systems of two linear equations algebraically/graphically
description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically, and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection. For example, 3x + 2y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 6 have no solution because 3x + 2y cannot simultaneously be 5 and 6.

domain: Expressions and Equations (8.EE)
skill: Solve real-world problems with systems of linear equations
description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to to linear equations in two variables. For example, given coordinates for two pairs of points, determine whether the line through the first pair of points intersects the line through the second pair.

domain: Functions (8.F)
skill: Understand a function as a rule with one output per input
description: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output. (Function notation is not required in grade 8.)

domain: Functions (8.F)
skill: Compare properties of two functions
description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). For example, given a linear function represented by a table of values and a linear function represented by an algebraic expression, determine which function has the greater rate of change.

domain: Functions (8.F)
skill: Interpret y = mx + b as a linear function
description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear. For example, the function A = s² giving the area of a square as a function of its side length is not linear because its graph contains the points (1,1), (2,4) and (3,9), which are not on a straight line.

domain: Functions (8.F)
skill: Construct a function to model a linear relationship
description: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

domain: Functions (8.F)
skill: Describe and sketch a function's qualitative behavior
description: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear). Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.

domain: Geometry (8.G)
skill: Verify properties of rotations, reflections, translations
description: Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations:

domain: Geometry (8.G)
skill: Lines map to lines of the same length
description: Lines are taken to lines, and line segments to line segments of the same length.

domain: Geometry (8.G)
skill: Angles map to angles of the same measure
description: Angles are taken to angles of the same measure.

domain: Geometry (8.G)
skill: Parallel lines map to parallel lines
description: Parallel lines are taken to parallel lines.

domain: Geometry (8.G)
skill: Understand congruence via rotations/reflections/translations
description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, and translations; given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.

domain: Geometry (8.G)
skill: Describe effect of transformations using coordinates
description: Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations, and reflections on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.

domain: Geometry (8.G)
skill: Understand similarity via transformations and dilations
description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, translations, and dilations; given two similar two-dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.

domain: Geometry (8.G)
skill: Establish facts about angle sums and similarity
description: Use informal arguments to establish facts about the angle sum and exterior angle of triangles, about the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and the angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles. For example, arrange three copies of the same triangle so that the sum of the three angles appears to form a line, and give an argument in terms of transversals why this is so.

domain: Geometry (8.G)
skill: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem
description: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.

domain: Geometry (8.G)
skill: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find side lengths
description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems in two and three dimensions.

domain: Geometry (8.G)
skill: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find distance between points
description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.

domain: Geometry (8.G)
skill: Know and use volume formulas for cones, cylinders, spheres
description: Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

domain: Statistics and Probability (8.SP)
skill: Construct and interpret scatter plots
description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

domain: Statistics and Probability (8.SP)
skill: Informally fit a straight line to scatter plot data
description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

domain: Statistics and Probability (8.SP)
skill: Use a linear model's equation to solve problems
description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept. For example, in a linear model for a biology experiment, interpret a slope of 1.5 cm/hr as meaning that an additional hour of sunlight each day is associated with an additional 1.5 cm in mature plant height.

domain: Statistics and Probability (8.SP)
skill: Interpret two-way tables of categorical data
description: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables. For example, collect data from students in your class on whether or not they have a curfew on school nights and whether or not they have assigned chores at home. Is there evidence that those who have a curfew also tend to have chores?

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Solve probability problems with finite sample spaces
description: Students solve probability problems with finite sample spaces by using the rules for addition, multiplication, and complementation for probability distributions and understand the simplifications that arise with independent events.

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Use conditional probability to solve for probabilities
description: Students know the definition of conditional probability and use it to solve for probabilities in finite sample spaces.

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Understand discrete random variables
description: Students demonstrate an understanding of the notion of discrete random variables by using this concept to solve for the probabilities of outcomes, such as the probability of the occurrence of five or fewer heads in 14 coin tosses.

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Interpret continuous random variable probability as area under a density curve
description: Students understand the notion of a continuous random variable and can interpret the probability of an outcome as the area of a region under the graph of the probability density function associated with the random variable.

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Determine the mean of a discrete random variable
description: Students know the definition of the mean of a discrete random variable and can determine the mean for a particular discrete random variable.

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Determine the variance of a discrete random variable
description: Students know the definition of the variance of a discrete random variable and can determine the variance for a particular discrete random variable.

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Use standard distributions to solve for events
description: Students demonstrate an understanding of the standard distributions (normal, binomial, and exponential) and can use the distributions to solve for events in problems in which the distribution belongs to those families.

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Determine mean/standard deviation of a normal random variable
description: Students determine the mean and the standard deviation of a normally distributed random variable.

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Apply the central limit theorem to binomial probability approximations
description: Students know the central limit theorem and can use it to obtain approximations for probabilities in problems of finite sample spaces in which the probabilities are distributed binomially.

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Compute mean, median, mode of a data distribution
description: Students know the definitions of the mean, median, and mode of distribution of data and can compute each of them in particular situations.

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Compute variance and standard deviation of a data distribution
description: Students compute the variance and the standard deviation of a distribution of data.

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Find a line of best fit using least squares regression
description: Students find the line of best fit to a given distribution of data by using least squares regression.

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Understand the correlation coefficient and its properties
description: Students know what the correlation coefficient of two variables means and are familiar with the coefficient’s properties.

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Organize and describe data distributions with multiple methods
description: Students organize and describe distributions of data by using a number of different methods, including frequency tables, histograms, standard line graphs and bar graphs, stem-and-leaf displays, scatterplots, and box-and-whisker plots.

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Understand statistics, sampling distributions, and variability of a statistic
description: Students are familiar with the notions of a statistic of a distribution of values, of the sampling distribution of a statistic, and of the variability of a statistic.

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Relate sampling distribution mean/SD to population mean/SD
description: Students know basic facts concerning the relation between the mean and the standard deviation of a sampling distribution and the mean and the standard deviation of the population distribution.

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Determine confidence intervals and required sample size
description: Students determine confidence intervals for a simple random sample from a normal distribution of data and determine the sample size required for a desired margin of error.

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Determine the P-value for a statistic
description: Students determine the P-value for a statistic for a simple random sample from a normal distribution.

domain: Advanced Placement Probability and Statistics
skill: Understand the chi-square distribution and test
description: Students are familiar with the chi-square distribution and chi-square test and understand their uses.

domain: Number and Quantity: The Real Number System (N-RN) — Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents
skill: Explain the meaning of rational exponents
description: Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents. For example, we define 5^(1/3) to be the cube root of 5 because we want (5^(1/3))^3 = 5^((1/3)·3) to hold, so (5^(1/3))^3 must equal 5.

domain: Number and Quantity: The Real Number System (N-RN) — Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents
skill: Rewrite expressions with radicals and rational exponents
description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

domain: Number and Quantity: The Real Number System (N-RN) — Use properties of rational and irrational numbers
skill: Explain closure properties of rational/irrational sums and products
description: Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is irrational.

domain: Number and Quantity: Quantities (N-Q) [Foundation for work with expressions, equations and functions] — Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems
skill: Use units to guide solving multi-step problems
description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

domain: Number and Quantity: Quantities (N-Q) [Foundation for work with expressions, equations and functions] — Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems
skill: Define appropriate quantities for descriptive modeling
description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

domain: Number and Quantity: Quantities (N-Q) [Foundation for work with expressions, equations and functions] — Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems
skill: Choose accuracy level appropriate to measurement limits
description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Linear, exponential, and quadratic] — Interpret the structure of expressions
skill: Interpret expressions representing a quantity in context
description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Linear, exponential, and quadratic] — Interpret the structure of expressions
skill: Interpret parts of an expression
description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Linear, exponential, and quadratic] — Interpret the structure of expressions
skill: Interpret an expression's parts as a single entity
description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity. For example, interpret P(1 + r)^n as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Linear, exponential, and quadratic] — Interpret the structure of expressions
skill: Use expression structure to rewrite it
description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Quadratic and exponential] — Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems
skill: Produce equivalent expression forms to reveal properties
description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Quadratic and exponential] — Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems
skill: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal zeros
description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Quadratic and exponential] — Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems
skill: Complete the square to reveal max/min value
description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Quadratic and exponential] — Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems
skill: Use exponent properties to transform exponential expressions
description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions. For example, the expression 1.15^t can be rewritten as (1.15^(1/12))^(12t) ≈ 1.012^(12t) to reveal the approximate equivalent monthly interest rate if the annual rate is 15%.

domain: Algebra: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions (A-APR) [Linear and quadratic] — Perform arithmetic operations on polynomials
skill: Understand polynomials form a closed system like integers
description: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

domain: Algebra: Creating Equations (A-CED) [Linear, quadratic, and exponential (integer inputs only); for A.CED.3 linear only] — Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
skill: Create equations/inequalities in one variable to solve problems
description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable including ones with absolute value and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions. CA

domain: Algebra: Creating Equations (A-CED) [Linear, quadratic, and exponential (integer inputs only); for A.CED.3 linear only] — Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
skill: Create and graph equations in two or more variables
description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

domain: Algebra: Creating Equations (A-CED) [Linear, quadratic, and exponential (integer inputs only); for A.CED.3 linear only] — Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
skill: Represent constraints and interpret solutions as viable/non-viable
description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context. For example, represent inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of different foods.

domain: Algebra: Creating Equations (A-CED) [Linear, quadratic, and exponential (integer inputs only); for A.CED.3 linear only] — Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
skill: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest
description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations. For example, rearrange Ohm’s law V = IR to highlight resistance R.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Master linear; learn as general principle] — Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning
skill: Explain each step of solving an equation as reasoning
description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Linear inequalities; literal equations that are linear in the variables being solved for; quadratics with real solutions] — Solve equations and inequalities in one variable
skill: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable
description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Linear inequalities; literal equations that are linear in the variables being solved for; quadratics with real solutions] — Solve equations and inequalities in one variable
skill: Solve one-variable absolute value equations/inequalities
description: Solve one-variable equations and inequalities involving absolute value, graphing the solutions and interpreting them in context. CA

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Linear inequalities; literal equations that are linear in the variables being solved for; quadratics with real solutions] — Solve equations and inequalities in one variable
skill: Solve quadratic equations in one variable
description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Linear inequalities; literal equations that are linear in the variables being solved for; quadratics with real solutions] — Solve equations and inequalities in one variable
skill: Derive the quadratic formula by completing the square
description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x – p)^2 = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Linear inequalities; literal equations that are linear in the variables being solved for; quadratics with real solutions] — Solve equations and inequalities in one variable
skill: Solve quadratic equations by various methods
description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x^2 = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula, and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Linear-linear and linear-quadratic] — Solve systems of equations
skill: Prove replacement of an equation preserves solutions
description: Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Linear-linear and linear-quadratic] — Solve systems of equations
skill: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately
description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Linear-linear and linear-quadratic] — Solve systems of equations
skill: Solve a linear-quadratic system algebraically/graphically
description: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Linear and exponential; learn as general principle] — Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically
skill: Understand a graph as the set of solutions to an equation
description: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Linear and exponential; learn as general principle] — Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically
skill: Explain intersection points as solutions to f(x)=g(x)
description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Linear and exponential; learn as general principle] — Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically
skill: Graph solutions to linear inequalities and systems
description: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Learn as general principle; focus on linear and exponential and on arithmetic and geometric sequences] — Understand the concept of a function and use function notation
skill: Understand a function assigns one range element per domain element
description: Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Learn as general principle; focus on linear and exponential and on arithmetic and geometric sequences] — Understand the concept of a function and use function notation
skill: Use function notation and evaluate functions
description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Learn as general principle; focus on linear and exponential and on arithmetic and geometric sequences] — Understand the concept of a function and use function notation
skill: Recognize sequences as functions with integer domains
description: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers. For example, the Fibonacci sequence is defined recursively by f(0) = f(1) = 1, f(n + 1) = f(n) + f(n − 1) for n ≥ 1.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Linear, exponential, and quadratic] — Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context
skill: Interpret key features of function graphs and tables
description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Linear, exponential, and quadratic] — Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context
skill: Relate a function's domain to its graph and context
description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes. For example, if the function h gives the number of person-hours it takes to assemble n engines in a factory, then the positive integers would be an appropriate domain for the function.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Linear, exponential, and quadratic] — Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context
skill: Calculate and interpret average rate of change
description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Linear, exponential, quadratic, absolute value, step, piecewise-defined] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Graph functions and show key features
description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Linear, exponential, quadratic, absolute value, step, piecewise-defined] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Graph linear/quadratic functions showing intercepts/max/min
description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Linear, exponential, quadratic, absolute value, step, piecewise-defined] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Graph root, piecewise, step, and absolute value functions
description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Linear, exponential, quadratic, absolute value, step, piecewise-defined] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Graph exponential, log, and trig functions
description: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior, and trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Linear, exponential, quadratic, absolute value, step, piecewise-defined] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Rewrite a function's expression to reveal properties
description: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Linear, exponential, quadratic, absolute value, step, piecewise-defined] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Factor/complete the square to show zeros and symmetry
description: Use the process of factoring and completing the square in a quadratic function to show zeros, extreme values, and symmetry of the graph, and interpret these in terms of a context.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Linear, exponential, quadratic, absolute value, step, piecewise-defined] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Interpret exponents to classify growth or decay
description: Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions. For example, identify percent rate of change in functions such as y = (1.02)^t, y = (0.97)^t, y = (1.01)^(12t), and y = (1.2)^(t/10), and classify them as representing exponential growth or decay.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Linear, exponential, quadratic, absolute value, step, piecewise-defined] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Compare properties of two functions in different representations
description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). For example, given a graph of one quadratic function and an algebraic expression for another, say which has the larger maximum.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [For F.BF.1, 2, linear, exponential, and quadratic] — Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities
skill: Write a function describing a relationship between quantities
description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [For F.BF.1, 2, linear, exponential, and quadratic] — Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities
skill: Determine an explicit expression or recursive process
description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [For F.BF.1, 2, linear, exponential, and quadratic] — Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities
skill: Combine standard function types with arithmetic operations
description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations. For example, build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [For F.BF.1, 2, linear, exponential, and quadratic] — Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities
skill: Write arithmetic/geometric sequences recursively and explicitly
description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [Linear, exponential, quadratic, and absolute value; for F.BF.4a, linear only] — Build new functions from existing functions
skill: Identify graph transformation effects of f(x)+k, kf(x), etc.
description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, kf(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [Linear, exponential, quadratic, and absolute value; for F.BF.4a, linear only] — Build new functions from existing functions
skill: Find inverse functions
description: Find inverse functions.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [Linear, exponential, quadratic, and absolute value; for F.BF.4a, linear only] — Build new functions from existing functions
skill: Solve f(x)=c and write the inverse expression
description: Solve an equation of the form f(x) = c for a simple function f that has an inverse and write an expression for the inverse.

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Distinguish linear from exponential situations
description: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and with exponential functions.

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Prove linear/exponential growth patterns over equal intervals
description: Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals, and that exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Recognize constant rate of change situations
description: Recognize situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another.

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Recognize constant percent rate situations
description: Recognize situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Construct linear/exponential functions from given data
description: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a table).

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Observe exponential growth exceeds linear/quadratic growth
description: Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial function.

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) [Linear and exponential of form f(x) = bx + k] — Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model
skill: Interpret parameters in a linear or exponential function
description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) — Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model
skill: Apply quadratic functions to physical problems
description: Apply quadratic functions to physical problems, such as the motion of an object under the force of gravity. CA

domain: Statistics and Probability: Interpreting Categorical and Quantitative Data (S-ID) — Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable
skill: Represent data with plots on the number line
description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

domain: Statistics and Probability: Interpreting Categorical and Quantitative Data (S-ID) — Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable
skill: Compare center and spread of two or more data sets
description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Interpreting Categorical and Quantitative Data (S-ID) — Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable
skill: Interpret differences in shape, center, spread accounting for outliers
description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

domain: Statistics and Probability: Interpreting Categorical and Quantitative Data (S-ID) [Linear focus; discuss general principle] — Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables
skill: Summarize categorical data in two-way frequency tables
description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Interpreting Categorical and Quantitative Data (S-ID) [Linear focus; discuss general principle] — Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables
skill: Represent and describe relationships on a scatter plot
description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Interpreting Categorical and Quantitative Data (S-ID) [Linear focus; discuss general principle] — Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables
skill: Fit a function to data and use it to solve problems
description: Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data. Use given functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear, quadratic, and exponential models.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Interpreting Categorical and Quantitative Data (S-ID) [Linear focus; discuss general principle] — Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables
skill: Assess model fit by analyzing residuals
description: Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Interpreting Categorical and Quantitative Data (S-ID) [Linear focus; discuss general principle] — Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables
skill: Fit a linear function to a scatter plot
description: Fit a linear function for a scatter plot that suggests a linear association.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Interpreting Categorical and Quantitative Data (S-ID) — Interpret linear models
skill: Interpret slope and intercept of a linear model
description: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Interpreting Categorical and Quantitative Data (S-ID) — Interpret linear models
skill: Compute and interpret the correlation coefficient
description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Interpreting Categorical and Quantitative Data (S-ID) — Interpret linear models
skill: Distinguish correlation from causation
description: Distinguish between correlation and causation.

domain: Number and Quantity: The Complex Number System (N-CN) — Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers
skill: Know the complex number i and form a + bi
description: Know there is a complex number i such that i² = −1, and every complex number has the form a + bi with a and b real.

domain: Number and Quantity: The Complex Number System (N-CN) — Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers
skill: Add, subtract, multiply complex numbers
description: Use the relation i² = −1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.

domain: Number and Quantity: The Complex Number System (N-CN) [Polynomials with real coefficients] — Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations
skill: Solve quadratic equations with complex solutions
description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.

domain: Number and Quantity: The Complex Number System (N-CN) [Polynomials with real coefficients] — Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations
skill: Extend polynomial identities to complex numbers
description: (+) Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers. For example, rewrite x² + 4 as (x + 2i)(x – 2i).

domain: Number and Quantity: The Complex Number System (N-CN) [Polynomials with real coefficients] — Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations
skill: Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
description: (+) Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; show that it is true for quadratic polynomials.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Polynomial and rational] — Interpret the structure of expressions
skill: Interpret expressions representing a quantity in context
description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Polynomial and rational] — Interpret the structure of expressions
skill: Interpret parts of an expression
description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Polynomial and rational] — Interpret the structure of expressions
skill: Interpret an expression's parts as a single entity
description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity. For example, interpret P(1 + r)^n as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Polynomial and rational] — Interpret the structure of expressions
skill: Use expression structure to rewrite it
description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) — Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems
skill: Derive and use the finite geometric series formula
description: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is not 1), and use the formula to solve problems. For example, calculate mortgage payments.

domain: Algebra: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions (A-APR) [Beyond quadratic] — Perform arithmetic operations on polynomials
skill: Understand polynomials form a closed system like integers
description: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

domain: Algebra: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions (A-APR) — Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials
skill: Apply the Remainder Theorem
description: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x – a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x – a) is a factor of p(x).

domain: Algebra: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions (A-APR) — Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials
skill: Identify zeros to construct a rough polynomial graph
description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

domain: Algebra: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions (A-APR) — Use polynomial identities to solve problems
skill: Prove and use polynomial identities
description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships. For example, the polynomial identity (x² + y²)² = (x² – y²)² + (2xy)² can be used to generate Pythagorean triples.

domain: Algebra: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions (A-APR) — Use polynomial identities to solve problems
skill: Apply the Binomial Theorem
description: (+) Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x + y)^n in powers of x and y for a positive integer n, where x and y are any numbers, with coefficients determined for example by Pascal’s Triangle. (The Binomial Theorem can be proved by mathematical induction or by a combinatorial argument.)

domain: Algebra: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions (A-APR) [Linear and quadratic denominators] — Rewrite rational expressions
skill: Rewrite rational expressions using division
description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

domain: Algebra: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions (A-APR) [Linear and quadratic denominators] — Rewrite rational expressions
skill: Add, subtract, multiply, divide rational expressions
description: (+) Understand that rational expressions form a system analogous to the rational numbers, closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational expression; add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions.

domain: Algebra: Creating Equations (A-CED) [Equations using all available types of expressions, including simple root functions] — Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
skill: Create equations/inequalities in one variable to solve problems
description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable including ones with absolute value and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions. CA

domain: Algebra: Creating Equations (A-CED) [Equations using all available types of expressions, including simple root functions] — Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
skill: Create and graph equations in two or more variables
description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

domain: Algebra: Creating Equations (A-CED) [Equations using all available types of expressions, including simple root functions] — Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
skill: Represent constraints and interpret solutions as viable/non-viable
description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context.

domain: Algebra: Creating Equations (A-CED) [Equations using all available types of expressions, including simple root functions] — Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
skill: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest
description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Simple radical and rational] — Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning
skill: Solve rational/radical equations and identify extraneous solutions
description: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) — Solve equations and inequalities in one variable
skill: Solve one-variable absolute value equations/inequalities
description: Solve one-variable equations and inequalities involving absolute value, graphing the solutions and interpreting them in context. CA

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Combine polynomial, rational, radical, absolute value, and exponential functions] — Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically
skill: Explain intersection points as solutions to f(x)=g(x)
description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Emphasize selection of appropriate models] — Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context
skill: Interpret key features of function graphs and tables
description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Emphasize selection of appropriate models] — Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context
skill: Relate a function's domain to its graph and context
description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Emphasize selection of appropriate models] — Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context
skill: Calculate and interpret average rate of change
description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Focus on using key features to guide selection of appropriate type of model function] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Graph functions and show key features
description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Focus on using key features to guide selection of appropriate type of model function] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Graph root, piecewise, step, and absolute value functions
description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Focus on using key features to guide selection of appropriate type of model function] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Graph polynomial functions showing zeros and end behavior
description: Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Focus on using key features to guide selection of appropriate type of model function] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Graph exponential, log, and trig functions
description: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior, and trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Focus on using key features to guide selection of appropriate type of model function] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Rewrite a function's expression to reveal properties
description: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Focus on using key features to guide selection of appropriate type of model function] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Compare properties of two functions in different representations
description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [Include all types of functions studied] — Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities
skill: Write a function describing a relationship between quantities
description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [Include all types of functions studied] — Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities
skill: Combine standard function types with arithmetic operations
description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations. For example, build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [Include simple radical, rational, and exponential functions; emphasize common effect of each transformation across function types] — Build new functions from existing functions
skill: Identify graph transformation effects of f(x)+k, kf(x), etc.
description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, kf(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [Include simple radical, rational, and exponential functions; emphasize common effect of each transformation across function types] — Build new functions from existing functions
skill: Find inverse functions
description: Find inverse functions.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [Include simple radical, rational, and exponential functions; emphasize common effect of each transformation across function types] — Build new functions from existing functions
skill: Solve f(x)=c and write the inverse expression
description: Solve an equation of the form f(x) = c for a simple function f that has an inverse and write an expression for the inverse. For example, f(x) = 2x³ or f(x) = (x + 1)/(x − 1) for x ≠ 1.

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) [Logarithms as solutions for exponentials] — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Express exponential model solutions as logarithms
description: For exponential models, express as a logarithm the solution to ab^(ct) = d where a, c, and d are numbers and the base b is 2, 10, or e; evaluate the logarithm using technology.

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Prove simple laws of logarithms
description: Prove simple laws of logarithms. CA

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Translate logarithms between bases
description: Use the definition of logarithms to translate between logarithms in any base. CA

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Use log properties to simplify and approximate expressions
description: Understand and use the properties of logarithms to simplify logarithmic numeric expressions and to identify their approximate values. CA

domain: Functions: Trigonometric Functions (F-TF) — Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle
skill: Understand radian measure as arc length on the unit circle
description: Understand radian measure of an angle as the length of the arc on the unit circle subtended by the angle.

domain: Functions: Trigonometric Functions (F-TF) — Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle
skill: Extend trig functions to all real numbers via the unit circle
description: Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise around the unit circle.

domain: Functions: Trigonometric Functions (F-TF) — Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle
skill: Graph all six basic trigonometric functions
description: Graph all 6 basic trigonometric functions. CA

domain: Functions: Trigonometric Functions (F-TF) — Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions
skill: Choose trig functions to model periodic phenomena
description: Choose trigonometric functions to model periodic phenomena with specified amplitude, frequency, and midline.

domain: Functions: Trigonometric Functions (F-TF) — Prove and apply trigonometric identities
skill: Prove and apply the Pythagorean trig identity
description: Prove the Pythagorean identity sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1 and use it to find sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) given sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) and the quadrant of the angle.

domain: Geometry: Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations (G-GPE) [In Algebra II, this standard addresses only circles and parabolas] — Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section
skill: Identify and graph conic sections from a general quadratic equation
description: Given a quadratic equation of the form ax² + by² + cx + dy + e = 0, use the method for completing the square to put the equation into standard form; identify whether the graph of the equation is a circle, ellipse, parabola, or hyperbola and graph the equation. CA

domain: Statistics and Probability: Interpreting Categorical and Quantitative Data (S-ID) — Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable
skill: Fit data to a normal distribution and estimate percentages
description: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal curve.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Making Inferences and Justifying Conclusions (S-IC) — Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments
skill: Understand statistics as inference about population parameters
description: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters based on a random sample from that population.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Making Inferences and Justifying Conclusions (S-IC) — Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments
skill: Decide if a model is consistent with a data-generating process
description: Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating process, e.g., using simulation. For example, a model says a spinning coin falls heads up with probability 0.5. Would a result of 5 tails in a row cause you to question the model?

domain: Statistics and Probability: Making Inferences and Justifying Conclusions (S-IC) — Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies
skill: Recognize purposes of surveys, experiments, observational studies
description: Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Making Inferences and Justifying Conclusions (S-IC) — Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies
skill: Estimate population mean/proportion and margin of error
description: Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error through the use of simulation models for random sampling.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Making Inferences and Justifying Conclusions (S-IC) — Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies
skill: Compare two treatments using randomized experiment data
description: Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to decide if differences between parameters are significant.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Making Inferences and Justifying Conclusions (S-IC) — Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies
skill: Evaluate reports based on data
description: Evaluate reports based on data.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Using Probability to Make Decisions (S-MD) [Include more complex situations] — Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions
skill: Use probabilities to make fair decisions
description: (+) Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g., drawing by lots, using a random number generator).

domain: Statistics and Probability: Using Probability to Make Decisions (S-MD) [Include more complex situations] — Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions
skill: Analyze decisions and strategies using probability
description: (+) Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g., product testing, medical testing, pulling a hockey goalie at the end of a game).

domain: Calculus
skill: Understand formal/graphical definition of limit
description: Students demonstrate knowledge of both the formal definition and the graphical interpretation of limit of values of functions. This knowledge includes one-sided limits, infinite limits, and limits at infinity. Students know the definition of convergence and divergence of a function as the domain variable approaches either a number or infinity:

domain: Calculus
skill: Prove and use limit theorems for combined functions
description: Students prove and use theorems evaluating the limits of sums, products, quotients, and composition of functions.

domain: Calculus
skill: Use graphical calculators to verify and estimate limits
description: Students use graphical calculators to verify and estimate limits.

domain: Calculus
skill: Prove and use special trigonometric limits
description: Students prove and use special limits, such as the limits of (sin(x))/x and (1−cos(x))/x as x tends to 0.

domain: Calculus
skill: Understand formal/graphical definition of continuity
description: Students demonstrate knowledge of both the formal definition and the graphical interpretation of continuity of a function.

domain: Calculus
skill: Apply the intermediate value and extreme value theorems
