description: Students demonstrate an understanding and the application of the intermediate value theorem and the extreme value theorem.

domain: Calculus
skill: Understand the formal definition of the derivative and differentiability
description: Students demonstrate an understanding of the formal definition of the derivative of a function at a point and the notion of differentiability:

domain: Calculus
skill: Understand the derivative as the slope of the tangent line
description: Students demonstrate an understanding of the derivative of a function as the slope of the tangent line to the graph of the function.

domain: Calculus
skill: Interpret the derivative as instantaneous rate of change
description: Students demonstrate an understanding of the interpretation of the derivative as an instantaneous rate of change. Students can use derivatives to solve a variety of problems from physics, chemistry, economics, and so forth that involve the rate of change of a function.

domain: Calculus
skill: Understand the relation between differentiability and continuity
description: Students understand the relation between differentiability and continuity.

domain: Calculus
skill: Derive and use derivative formulas for common function types
description: Students derive derivative formulas and use them to find the derivatives of algebraic, trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

domain: Calculus
skill: Know and apply the chain rule
description: Students know the chain rule and its proof and applications to the calculation of the derivative of a variety of composite functions.

domain: Calculus
skill: Find derivatives of parametric functions and use implicit differentiation
description: Students find the derivatives of parametrically defined functions and use implicit differentiation in a wide variety of problems in physics, chemistry, economics, and so forth.

domain: Calculus
skill: Compute higher-order derivatives
description: Students compute derivatives of higher orders.

domain: Calculus
skill: Apply Rolle's Theorem, the Mean Value Theorem, and L'Hopital's rule
description: Students know and can apply Rolle’s Theorem, the mean value theorem, and L’Hôpital’s rule.

domain: Calculus
skill: Use differentiation to sketch graphs by hand
description: Students use differentiation to sketch, by hand, graphs of functions. They can identify maxima, minima, inflection points, and intervals in which the function is increasing and decreasing.

domain: Calculus
skill: Know Newton's method for approximating zeros
description: Students know Newton’s method for approximating the zeros of a function.

domain: Calculus
skill: Use differentiation to solve optimization problems
description: Students use differentiation to solve optimization (maximum-minimum problems) in a variety of pure and applied contexts.

domain: Calculus
skill: Use differentiation to solve related rate problems
description: Students use differentiation to solve related rate problems in a variety of pure and applied contexts.

domain: Calculus
skill: Define and approximate the definite integral using Riemann sums
description: Students know the definition of the definite integral by using Riemann sums. They use this definition to approximate integrals.

domain: Calculus
skill: Apply the definition of the integral to model applied problems
description: Students apply the definition of the integral to model problems in physics, economics, and so forth, obtaining results in terms of integrals.

domain: Calculus
skill: Prove and use the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
description: Students demonstrate knowledge and proof of the fundamental theorem of calculus and use it to interpret integrals as antiderivatives.

domain: Calculus
skill: Use definite integrals for area, velocity, volume, and work
description: Students use definite integrals in problems involving area, velocity, acceleration, volume of a solid, area of a surface of revolution, length of a curve, and work.

domain: Calculus
skill: Compute integrals using substitution, parts, and trig substitution
description: Students compute, by hand, the integrals of a wide variety of functions by using techniques of integration, such as substitution, integration by parts, and trigonometric substitution. They can also combine these techniques when appropriate.

domain: Calculus
skill: Know properties of inverse trig functions as indefinite integrals
description: Students know the definitions and properties of inverse trigonometric functions and the expression of these functions as indefinite integrals.

domain: Calculus
skill: Compute integrals of rational functions using partial fractions
description: Students compute, by hand, the integrals of rational functions by combining the techniques in standard 17.0 with the algebraic techniques of partial fractions and completing the square.

domain: Calculus
skill: Compute integrals of trigonometric functions
description: Students compute the integrals of trigonometric functions by using the techniques noted above.

domain: Calculus
skill: Approximate integrals numerically using Simpson's rule and Newton's method
description: Students understand the algorithms involved in Simpson’s rule and Newton’s method. They use calculators or computers or both to approximate integrals numerically.

domain: Calculus
skill: Understand improper integrals as limits of definite integrals
description: Students understand improper integrals as limits of definite integrals.

domain: Calculus
skill: Determine convergence/divergence of sequences and series
description: Students demonstrate an understanding of the definitions of convergence and divergence of sequences and series of real numbers. By using such tests as the comparison test, ratio test, and alternate series test, they can determine whether a series converges.

domain: Calculus
skill: Compute the radius of convergence of power series
description: Students understand and can compute the radius (interval) of the convergence of power series.

domain: Calculus
skill: Differentiate and integrate power series term by term
description: Students differentiate and integrate the terms of a power series in order to form new series from known ones.

domain: Calculus
skill: Calculate Taylor polynomials and Taylor series
description: Students calculate Taylor polynomials and Taylor series of basic functions, including the remainder term.

domain: Calculus
skill: Solve elementary differential equations including growth-and-decay problems
description: Students know the techniques of solution of selected elementary differential equations and their applications to a wide variety of situations, including growth-and-decay problems.

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) — Experiment with transformations in the plane
skill: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, line, etc.
description: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment, based on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) — Experiment with transformations in the plane
skill: Represent transformations as functions of points
description: Represent transformations in the plane using, e.g., transparencies and geometry software; describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs and give other points as outputs. Compare transformations that preserve distance and angle to those that do not (e.g., translation versus horizontal stretch).

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) — Experiment with transformations in the plane
skill: Describe rotations/reflections carrying a polygon onto itself
description: Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations and reflections that carry it onto itself.

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) — Experiment with transformations in the plane
skill: Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, translations
description: Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles, perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) — Experiment with transformations in the plane
skill: Draw transformed figures and specify transformation sequences
description: Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the transformed figure using, e.g., graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software. Specify a sequence of transformations that will carry a given figure onto another.

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) [Build on rigid motions as a familiar starting point for development of concept of geometric proof] — Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions
skill: Use rigid motions to decide if figures are congruent
description: Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect of a given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) [Build on rigid motions as a familiar starting point for development of concept of geometric proof] — Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions
skill: Show triangle congruence via corresponding parts
description: Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are congruent.

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) [Build on rigid motions as a familiar starting point for development of concept of geometric proof] — Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions
skill: Explain ASA/SAS/SSS from the definition of congruence
description: Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, and SSS) follow from the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions.

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) [Focus on validity of underlying reasoning while using variety of ways of writing proofs] — Prove geometric theorems
skill: Prove theorems about lines and angles
description: Prove theorems about lines and angles. Theorems include: vertical angles are congruent; when a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent and corresponding angles are congruent; points on a perpendicular bisector of a line segment are exactly those equidistant from the segment’s endpoints.

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) [Focus on validity of underlying reasoning while using variety of ways of writing proofs] — Prove geometric theorems
skill: Prove theorems about triangles
description: Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: measures of interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°; base angles of isosceles triangles are congruent; the segment joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half the length; the medians of a triangle meet at a point.

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) [Focus on validity of underlying reasoning while using variety of ways of writing proofs] — Prove geometric theorems
skill: Prove theorems about parallelograms
description: Prove theorems about parallelograms. Theorems include: opposite sides are congruent, opposite angles are congruent, the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, and conversely, rectangles are parallelograms with congruent diagonals.

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) [Formalize and explain processes] — Make geometric constructions
skill: Make formal geometric constructions with various tools
description: Make formal geometric constructions with a variety of tools and methods (compass and straightedge, string, reflective devices, paper folding, dynamic geometric software, etc.). Copying a segment; copying an angle; bisecting a segment; bisecting an angle; constructing perpendicular lines, including the perpendicular bisector of a line segment; and constructing a line parallel to a given line through a point not on the line.

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) [Formalize and explain processes] — Make geometric constructions
skill: Construct an inscribed equilateral triangle, square, hexagon
description: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.

domain: Geometry: Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry (G-SRT) — Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations
skill: Verify properties of dilations
description: Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a center and a scale factor:

domain: Geometry: Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry (G-SRT) — Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations
skill: Understand dilation effect on lines through/not through center
description: A dilation takes a line not passing through the center of the dilation to a parallel line, and leaves a line passing through the center unchanged.

domain: Geometry: Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry (G-SRT) — Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations
skill: Understand dilation effect on segment length
description: The dilation of a line segment is longer or shorter in the ratio given by the scale factor.

domain: Geometry: Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry (G-SRT) — Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations
skill: Use similarity transformations to decide if figures are similar
description: Given two figures, use the definition of similarity in terms of similarity transformations to decide if they are similar; explain using similarity transformations the meaning of similarity for triangles as the equality of all corresponding pairs of angles and the proportionality of all corresponding pairs of sides.

domain: Geometry: Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry (G-SRT) — Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations
skill: Establish the AA criterion for triangle similarity
description: Use the properties of similarity transformations to establish the Angle-Angle (AA) criterion for two triangles to be similar.

domain: Geometry: Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry (G-SRT) — Prove theorems involving similarity
skill: Prove theorems about triangles using similarity
description: Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two proportionally, and conversely; the Pythagorean Theorem proved using triangle similarity.

domain: Geometry: Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry (G-SRT) — Prove theorems involving similarity
skill: Use congruence/similarity criteria to solve problems
description: Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures.

domain: Geometry: Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry (G-SRT) — Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles
skill: Understand trig ratios as properties of triangle angles
description: Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles in the triangle, leading to definitions of trigonometric ratios for acute angles.

domain: Geometry: Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry (G-SRT) — Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles
skill: Use the relationship between sine and cosine of complementary angles
description: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.

domain: Geometry: Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry (G-SRT) — Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles
skill: Use trig ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles
description: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.

domain: Geometry: Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry (G-SRT) — Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles
skill: Derive trig ratios for special right triangles
description: Derive and use the trigonometric ratios for special right triangles (30°, 60°, 90° and 45°, 45°, 90°). CA

domain: Geometry: Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry (G-SRT) — Apply trigonometry to general triangles
skill: Derive the triangle area formula using sine
description: (+) Derive the formula A = 1/2 ab sin(C) for the area of a triangle by drawing an auxiliary line from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side.

domain: Geometry: Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry (G-SRT) — Apply trigonometry to general triangles
skill: Prove and use the Laws of Sines and Cosines
description: (+) Prove the Laws of Sines and Cosines and use them to solve problems.

domain: Geometry: Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry (G-SRT) — Apply trigonometry to general triangles
skill: Apply Law of Sines/Cosines to find unknown measurements
description: (+) Understand and apply the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines to find unknown measurements in right and non-right triangles (e.g., surveying problems, resultant forces).

domain: Geometry: Circles (G-C) — Understand and apply theorems about circles
skill: Prove all circles are similar
description: Prove that all circles are similar.

domain: Geometry: Circles (G-C) — Understand and apply theorems about circles
skill: Identify relationships among inscribed angles, radii, chords
description: Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords. Include the relationship between central, inscribed, and circumscribed angles; inscribed angles on a diameter are right angles; the radius of a circle is perpendicular to the tangent where the radius intersects the circle.

domain: Geometry: Circles (G-C) — Understand and apply theorems about circles
skill: Construct inscribed/circumscribed circles of a triangle
description: Construct the inscribed and circumscribed circles of a triangle, and prove properties of angles for a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle.

domain: Geometry: Circles (G-C) — Understand and apply theorems about circles
skill: Construct a tangent line from an external point
description: (+) Construct a tangent line from a point outside a given circle to the circle.

domain: Geometry: Circles (G-C) [Radian introduced only as unit of measure] — Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles

description: Derive using similarity the fact that the length of the arc intercepted by an angle is proportional to the radius, and define the radian measure of the angle as the constant of proportionality; derive the formula for the area of a sector. Convert between degrees and radians. CA

domain: Geometry: Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations (G-GPE) — Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section
skill: Derive the equation of a circle
description: Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean Theorem; complete the square to find the center and radius of a circle given by an equation.

domain: Geometry: Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations (G-GPE) — Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section
skill: Derive the equation of a parabola
description: Derive the equation of a parabola given a focus and directrix.

domain: Geometry: Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations (G-GPE) [Include distance formula; relate to Pythagorean Theorem] — Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically
skill: Use coordinates to prove geometric theorems algebraically
description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically. For example, prove or disprove that a figure defined by four given points in the coordinate plane is a rectangle; prove or disprove that the point (1, √3) lies on the circle centered at the origin and containing the point (0, 2).

domain: Geometry: Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations (G-GPE) [Include distance formula; relate to Pythagorean Theorem] — Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically
skill: Prove slope criteria for parallel/perpendicular lines
description: Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to solve geometric problems (e.g., find the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that passes through a given point).

domain: Geometry: Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations (G-GPE) [Include distance formula; relate to Pythagorean Theorem] — Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically
skill: Find a point that partitions a segment in a given ratio
description: Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the segment in a given ratio.

domain: Geometry: Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations (G-GPE) [Include distance formula; relate to Pythagorean Theorem] — Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically
skill: Use coordinates to compute perimeters and areas
description: Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles, e.g., using the distance formula.

domain: Geometry: Geometric Measurement and Dimension (G-GMD) — Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems
skill: Give informal arguments for circumference/area/volume formulas
description: Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone. Use dissection arguments, Cavalieri’s principle, and informal limit arguments.

domain: Geometry: Geometric Measurement and Dimension (G-GMD) — Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems
skill: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, spheres
description: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.

domain: Geometry: Geometric Measurement and Dimension (G-GMD) — Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional objects
skill: Identify 2D cross-sections and 3D rotational objects
description: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

domain: Geometry: Geometric Measurement and Dimension (G-GMD) — Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional objects
skill: Determine effect of scale factor on length, area, volume
description: Know that the effect of a scale factor k greater than zero on length, area, and volume is to multiply each by k, k², and k³, respectively; determine length, area and volume measures using scale factors. CA

domain: Geometry: Geometric Measurement and Dimension (G-GMD) — Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional objects
skill: Verify triangle side/angle inequality relationships
description: Verify experimentally that in a triangle, angles opposite longer sides are larger, sides opposite larger angles are longer, and the sum of any two side lengths is greater than the remaining side length; apply these relationships to solve real-world and mathematical problems. CA

domain: Geometry: Modeling with Geometry (G-MG) — Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations
skill: Use geometric shapes and measures to describe objects
description: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g., modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).

domain: Geometry: Modeling with Geometry (G-MG) — Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations
skill: Apply density concepts in modeling situations
description: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g., persons per square mile, BTUs per cubic foot).

domain: Geometry: Modeling with Geometry (G-MG) — Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations
skill: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems
description: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems based on ratios).

domain: Statistics and Probability: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability (S-CP) [Link to data from simulations or experiments] — Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data
skill: Describe events as subsets of a sample space
description: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events (“or,” “and,” “not”).

domain: Statistics and Probability: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability (S-CP) [Link to data from simulations or experiments] — Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data
skill: Determine independence of two events
description: Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if they are independent.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability (S-CP) [Link to data from simulations or experiments] — Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data
skill: Understand conditional probability and independence
description: Understand the conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B), and interpret independence of A and B as saying that the conditional probability of A given B is the same as the probability of A, and the conditional probability of B given A is the same as the probability of B.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability (S-CP) [Link to data from simulations or experiments] — Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data
skill: Construct/interpret two-way frequency tables
description: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities. For example, collect data from a random sample of students in your school on their favorite subject among math, science, and English. Estimate the probability that a randomly selected student from your school will favor science given that the student is in tenth grade. Do the same for other subjects and compare the results.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability (S-CP) [Link to data from simulations or experiments] — Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data
skill: Explain conditional probability/independence in everyday terms
description: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability (S-CP) — Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model
skill: Find conditional probability as a fraction of outcomes
description: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B’s outcomes that also belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability (S-CP) — Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model
skill: Apply the Addition Rule for probability
description: Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) – P(A and B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability (S-CP) — Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model
skill: Apply the general Multiplication Rule
description: (+) Apply the general Multiplication Rule in a uniform probability model, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B|A) = P(B)P(A|B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability (S-CP) — Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model
skill: Use permutations/combinations for compound event probabilities
description: (+) Use permutations and combinations to compute probabilities of compound events and solve problems.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Using Probability to Make Decisions (S-MD) [Introductory; apply counting rules] — Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions
skill: Use probabilities to make fair decisions
description: (+) Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g., drawing by lots, using a random number generator).

domain: Statistics and Probability: Using Probability to Make Decisions (S-MD) [Introductory; apply counting rules] — Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions
skill: Analyze decisions and strategies using probability
description: (+) Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g., product testing, medical testing, pulling a hockey goalie at the end of a game).

domain: Counting and Cardinality (K.CC)
skill: Count to 100 by ones and tens
description: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.

domain: Counting and Cardinality (K.CC)
skill: Count forward from a given number
description: Count forward beginning from a given number within the known sequence (instead of having to begin at 1).

domain: Counting and Cardinality (K.CC)
skill: Write numbers 0-20
description: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0–20 (with 0 representing a count of no objects).

domain: Counting and Cardinality (K.CC)
skill: Connect counting to cardinality
description: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality.

domain: Counting and Cardinality (K.CC)
skill: Pair each object with one number name
description: When counting objects, say the number names in the standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object.

domain: Counting and Cardinality (K.CC)
skill: Understand last number name tells total
description: Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted. The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted.

domain: Counting and Cardinality (K.CC)
skill: Understand each successive number is one more
description: Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger.

domain: Counting and Cardinality (K.CC)
skill: Count to answer "how many?" questions
description: Count to answer “how many?” questions about as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle, or as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration; given a number from 1–20, count out that many objects.

domain: Counting and Cardinality (K.CC)
skill: Compare group sizes using matching/counting
description: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group, e.g., by using matching and counting strategies. (Includes groups with up to ten objects.)

domain: Counting and Cardinality (K.CC)
skill: Compare two numbers as written numerals
description: Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals.

domain: Operations and Algebraic Thinking (K.OA)
skill: Represent addition and subtraction multiple ways
description: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g., claps), acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.

domain: Operations and Algebraic Thinking (K.OA)
skill: Solve add/subtract word problems within 10
description: Solve addition and subtraction word problems, and add and subtract within 10, e.g., by using objects or drawings to represent the problem.

domain: Operations and Algebraic Thinking (K.OA)
skill: Decompose numbers into pairs multiple ways
description: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1).

domain: Operations and Algebraic Thinking (K.OA)
skill: Find the number that makes 10
description: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record the answer with a drawing or equation.

domain: Operations and Algebraic Thinking (K.OA)
skill: Fluently add and subtract within 5
description: Fluently add and subtract within 5.

domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten (K.NBT)
skill: Compose/decompose numbers 11-19
description: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each composition or decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 18 = 10 + 8); understand that these numbers are composed of ten ones and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

domain: Measurement and Data (K.MD)
skill: Describe measurable attributes of objects
description: Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight. Describe several measurable attributes of a single object.

domain: Measurement and Data (K.MD)
skill: Directly compare two objects' attributes
description: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has “more of”/“less of” the attribute, and describe the difference. For example, directly compare the heights of two children and describe one child as taller/shorter.

domain: Measurement and Data (K.MD)
skill: Classify objects and count by category
description: Classify objects into given categories; count the numbers of objects in each category and sort the categories by count. (Limit category counts to be less than or equal to 10.)

domain: Geometry (K.G)
skill: Describe objects using shape names and position
description: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next to.

domain: Geometry (K.G)
skill: Name shapes regardless of size/orientation
description: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.

domain: Geometry (K.G)
skill: Identify shapes as two- or three-dimensional
description: Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, “flat”) or three-dimensional (“solid”).

domain: Geometry (K.G)
skill: Analyze and compare 2D and 3D shapes
description: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g., number of sides and vertices/“corners”) and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).

domain: Geometry (K.G)
skill: Model shapes by building and drawing
description: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g., sticks and clay balls) and drawing shapes.

domain: Geometry (K.G)
skill: Compose simple shapes into larger shapes
description: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes. For example, “Can you join these two triangles with full sides touching to make a rectangle?”

domain: Number and Quantity: Quantities (N-Q) [Foundation for work with expressions, equations, and functions] — Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems
skill: Use units to guide solving multi-step problems
description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

domain: Number and Quantity: Quantities (N-Q) [Foundation for work with expressions, equations, and functions] — Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems
skill: Define appropriate quantities for descriptive modeling
description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

domain: Number and Quantity: Quantities (N-Q) [Foundation for work with expressions, equations, and functions] — Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems
skill: Choose accuracy level appropriate to measurement limits
description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Linear expressions and exponential expressions with integer exponents] — Interpret the structure of expressions
skill: Interpret expressions representing a quantity in context
description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Linear expressions and exponential expressions with integer exponents] — Interpret the structure of expressions
skill: Interpret parts of an expression
description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Linear expressions and exponential expressions with integer exponents] — Interpret the structure of expressions
skill: Interpret an expression's parts as a single entity
description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity. For example, interpret P(1 + r)^n as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.

domain: Algebra: Creating Equations (A-CED) [Linear and exponential (integer inputs only); for A.CED.3, linear only] — Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
skill: Create equations/inequalities in one variable to solve problems
description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable including ones with absolute value and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions. CA

domain: Algebra: Creating Equations (A-CED) [Linear and exponential (integer inputs only); for A.CED.3, linear only] — Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
skill: Create and graph equations in two or more variables
description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

domain: Algebra: Creating Equations (A-CED) [Linear and exponential (integer inputs only); for A.CED.3, linear only] — Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
skill: Represent constraints and interpret solutions as viable/non-viable
description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context. For example, represent inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of different foods.

domain: Algebra: Creating Equations (A-CED) [Linear and exponential (integer inputs only); for A.CED.3, linear only] — Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
skill: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest
description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations. For example, rearrange Ohm’s law V = IR to highlight resistance R.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Master linear; learn as general principle] — Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning
skill: Explain each step of solving an equation as reasoning
description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Linear inequalities; literal equations that are linear in the variables being solved for; exponential of a form, such as 2^x = 1/16] — Solve equations and inequalities in one variable
skill: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable
description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Linear inequalities; literal equations that are linear in the variables being solved for; exponential of a form, such as 2^x = 1/16] — Solve equations and inequalities in one variable
skill: Solve one-variable absolute value equations/inequalities
description: Solve one-variable equations and inequalities involving absolute value, graphing the solutions and interpreting them in context. CA

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Linear systems] — Solve systems of equations
skill: Prove replacement of an equation preserves solutions
description: Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Linear systems] — Solve systems of equations
skill: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately
description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Linear and exponential; learn as general principle] — Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically
skill: Understand a graph as the set of solutions to an equation
description: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Linear and exponential; learn as general principle] — Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically
skill: Explain intersection points as solutions to f(x)=g(x)
description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Linear and exponential; learn as general principle] — Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically
skill: Graph solutions to linear inequalities and systems
description: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Learn as general principle. Focus on linear and exponential (integer domains) and on arithmetic and geometric sequences] — Understand the concept of a function and use function notation
skill: Understand a function assigns one range element per domain element
description: Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Learn as general principle. Focus on linear and exponential (integer domains) and on arithmetic and geometric sequences] — Understand the concept of a function and use function notation
skill: Use function notation and evaluate functions
description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Learn as general principle. Focus on linear and exponential (integer domains) and on arithmetic and geometric sequences] — Understand the concept of a function and use function notation
skill: Recognize sequences as functions with integer domains
description: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers. For example, the Fibonacci sequence is defined recursively by f(0) = f(1) = 1, f(n + 1) = f(n) + f(n − 1) for n ≥ 1.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Linear and exponential (linear domain)] — Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context
skill: Interpret key features of function graphs and tables
description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Linear and exponential (linear domain)] — Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context
skill: Relate a function's domain to its graph and context
description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes. For example, if the function h gives the number of person-hours it takes to assemble n engines in a factory, then the positive integers would be an appropriate domain for the function.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Linear and exponential (linear domain)] — Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context
skill: Calculate and interpret average rate of change
description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Linear and exponential] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Graph functions and show key features
description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Linear and exponential] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Graph linear/quadratic functions showing intercepts/max/min
description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Linear and exponential] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Graph exponential, log, and trig functions
description: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior, and trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Linear and exponential] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Compare properties of two functions in different representations
description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [For F.BF.1, 2, linear and exponential (integer inputs)] — Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities
skill: Write a function describing a relationship between quantities
description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [For F.BF.1, 2, linear and exponential (integer inputs)] — Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities
skill: Determine an explicit expression or recursive process
description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [For F.BF.1, 2, linear and exponential (integer inputs)] — Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities
skill: Combine standard function types with arithmetic operations
description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations. For example, build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [For F.BF.1, 2, linear and exponential (integer inputs)] — Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities
skill: Write arithmetic/geometric sequences recursively and explicitly
description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [Linear and exponential; focus on vertical translations for exponential] — Build new functions from existing functions
skill: Identify graph transformation effects of f(x)+k, kf(x), etc.
description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, kf(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) [Linear and exponential] — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Distinguish linear from exponential situations
description: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and with exponential functions.

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) [Linear and exponential] — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Prove linear/exponential growth patterns over equal intervals
description: Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals, and that exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) [Linear and exponential] — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Recognize constant rate of change situations
description: Recognize situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another.

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) [Linear and exponential] — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Recognize constant percent rate situations
description: Recognize situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) [Linear and exponential] — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Construct linear/exponential functions from given data
description: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a table).

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) [Linear and exponential] — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Observe exponential growth exceeds linear/quadratic growth
description: Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial function.

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) [Linear and exponential of form f(x) = bx + k] — Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model
skill: Interpret parameters in a linear or exponential function
description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) — Experiment with transformations in the plane
skill: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, line, etc.
description: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment, based on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) — Experiment with transformations in the plane
skill: Represent transformations as functions of points
description: Represent transformations in the plane using, e.g., transparencies and geometry software; describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs and give other points as outputs. Compare transformations that preserve distance and angle to those that do not (e.g., translation versus horizontal stretch).

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) — Experiment with transformations in the plane
skill: Describe rotations/reflections carrying a polygon onto itself
description: Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations and reflections that carry it onto itself.

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) — Experiment with transformations in the plane
skill: Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, translations
description: Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles, perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) — Experiment with transformations in the plane
skill: Draw transformed figures and specify transformation sequences
description: Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the transformed figure using, e.g., graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software. Specify a sequence of transformations that will carry a given figure onto another.

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) [Build on rigid motions as a familiar starting point for development of concept of geometric proof] — Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions
skill: Use rigid motions to decide if figures are congruent
description: Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect of a given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.

domain: Geometry: Congruence (G-CO) [Build on rigid motions as a familiar starting point for development of concept of geometric proof] — Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions
skill: Show triangle congruence via corresponding parts
description: Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are congruent.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability (S-CP) — Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model
skill: Apply the general Multiplication Rule
description: (+) Apply the general Multiplication Rule in a uniform probability model, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B|A) = P(B)P(A|B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability (S-CP) — Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model
skill: Use permutations/combinations for compound event probabilities
description: (+) Use permutations and combinations to compute probabilities of compound events and solve problems.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Using Probability to Make Decisions (S-MD) [Introductory; apply counting rules] — Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions
skill: Use probabilities to make fair decisions

domain: Statistics and Probability: Using Probability to Make Decisions (S-MD) [Introductory; apply counting rules] — Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions
skill: Analyze decisions and strategies using probability
description: (+) Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g., product testing, medical testing, pulling a hockey goalie at the end of a game).

domain: Number and Quantity: The Complex Number System (N-CN) [Polynomials with real coefficients; apply N.CN.9 to higher degree polynomials] — Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations
skill: Extend polynomial identities to complex numbers
description: (+) Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers.

domain: Number and Quantity: The Complex Number System (N-CN) [Polynomials with real coefficients; apply N.CN.9 to higher degree polynomials] — Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations
skill: Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
description: (+) Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; show that it is true for quadratic polynomials.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Polynomial and rational] — Interpret the structure of expressions
skill: Interpret expressions representing a quantity in context
description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Polynomial and rational] — Interpret the structure of expressions
skill: Interpret parts of an expression
description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Polynomial and rational] — Interpret the structure of expressions
skill: Interpret an expression's parts as a single entity
description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) [Polynomial and rational] — Interpret the structure of expressions
skill: Use expression structure to rewrite it
description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

domain: Algebra: Seeing Structure in Expressions (A-SSE) — Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems
skill: Derive and use the finite geometric series formula
description: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is not 1), and use the formula to solve problems. For example, calculate mortgage payments.

domain: Algebra: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions (A-APR) [Beyond quadratic] — Perform arithmetic operations on polynomials
skill: Understand polynomials form a closed system like integers
description: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

domain: Algebra: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions (A-APR) — Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials
skill: Apply the Remainder Theorem
description: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x – a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x – a) is a factor of p(x).

domain: Algebra: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions (A-APR) — Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials
skill: Identify zeros to construct a rough polynomial graph
description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

domain: Algebra: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions (A-APR) — Use polynomial identities to solve problems
skill: Prove and use polynomial identities
description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships. For example, the polynomial identity (x² + y²)² = (x² – y²)² + (2xy)² can be used to generate Pythagorean triples.

domain: Algebra: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions (A-APR) — Use polynomial identities to solve problems
skill: Apply the Binomial Theorem
description: (+) Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x + y)^n in powers of x and y for a positive integer n, where x and y are any numbers, with coefficients determined for example by Pascal’s Triangle. (The Binomial Theorem may be proven by mathematical induction or by a combinatorial argument.)

domain: Algebra: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions (A-APR) [Linear and quadratic denominators] — Rewrite rational expressions
skill: Rewrite rational expressions using division
description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

domain: Algebra: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions (A-APR) [Linear and quadratic denominators] — Rewrite rational expressions
skill: Add, subtract, multiply, divide rational expressions
description: (+) Understand that rational expressions form a system analogous to the rational numbers, closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational expression; add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions.

domain: Algebra: Creating Equations (A-CED) [Equations using all available types of expressions, including simple root functions] — Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
skill: Create equations/inequalities in one variable to solve problems
description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable including ones with absolute value and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions. CA

domain: Algebra: Creating Equations (A-CED) [Equations using all available types of expressions, including simple root functions] — Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
skill: Create and graph equations in two or more variables
description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

domain: Algebra: Creating Equations (A-CED) [Equations using all available types of expressions, including simple root functions] — Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
skill: Represent constraints and interpret solutions as viable/non-viable
description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context. For example, represent inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of different foods.

domain: Algebra: Creating Equations (A-CED) [Equations using all available types of expressions, including simple root functions] — Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
skill: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest
description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Simple radical and rational] — Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning
skill: Solve rational/radical equations and identify extraneous solutions
description: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.

domain: Algebra: Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities (A-REI) [Combine polynomial, rational, radical, absolute value, and exponential functions] — Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically
skill: Explain intersection points as solutions to f(x)=g(x)
description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Include rational, square root and cube root; emphasize selection of appropriate models] — Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context
skill: Interpret key features of function graphs and tables
description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Include rational, square root and cube root; emphasize selection of appropriate models] — Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context
skill: Relate a function's domain to its graph and context
description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Include rational, square root and cube root; emphasize selection of appropriate models] — Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context
skill: Calculate and interpret average rate of change
description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Include rational and radical; focus on using key features to guide selection of appropriate type of model function] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Graph functions and show key features
description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Include rational and radical; focus on using key features to guide selection of appropriate type of model function] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Graph root, piecewise, step, and absolute value functions
description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Include rational and radical; focus on using key features to guide selection of appropriate type of model function] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Graph polynomial functions showing zeros and end behavior
description: Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Include rational and radical; focus on using key features to guide selection of appropriate type of model function] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Graph exponential, log, and trig functions
description: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior, and trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Include rational and radical; focus on using key features to guide selection of appropriate type of model function] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Rewrite a function's expression to reveal properties
description: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.

domain: Functions: Interpreting Functions (F-IF) [Include rational and radical; focus on using key features to guide selection of appropriate type of model function] — Analyze functions using different representations
skill: Compare properties of two functions in different representations
description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [Include all types of functions studied] — Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities
skill: Write a function describing a relationship between quantities
description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [Include all types of functions studied] — Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities
skill: Combine standard function types with arithmetic operations
description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations. For example, build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [Include simple, radical, rational, and exponential functions; emphasize common effect of each transformation across function types] — Build new functions from existing functions
skill: Identify graph transformation effects of f(x)+k, kf(x), etc.
description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, kf(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [Include simple, radical, rational, and exponential functions; emphasize common effect of each transformation across function types] — Build new functions from existing functions
skill: Find inverse functions
description: Find inverse functions.

domain: Functions: Building Functions (F-BF) [Include simple, radical, rational, and exponential functions; emphasize common effect of each transformation across function types] — Build new functions from existing functions
skill: Solve f(x)=c and write the inverse expression
description: Solve an equation of the form f(x) = c for a simple function f that has an inverse and write an expression for the inverse. For example, f(x) = (x + 1)/(x − 1) for x ≠ 1.

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) [Logarithms as solutions for exponentials] — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Express exponential model solutions as logarithms
description: For exponential models, express as a logarithm the solution to ab^(ct) = d where a, c, and d are numbers and the base b is 2, 10, or e; evaluate the logarithm using technology.

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Prove simple laws of logarithms
description: Prove simple laws of logarithms. CA

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Translate logarithms between bases
description: Use the definition of logarithms to translate between logarithms in any base. CA

domain: Functions: Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models (F-LE) — Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
skill: Use log properties to simplify and approximate expressions
description: Understand and use the properties of logarithms to simplify logarithmic numeric expressions and to identify their approximate values. CA

domain: Functions: Trigonometric Functions (F-TF) — Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle
skill: Understand radian measure as arc length on the unit circle
description: Understand radian measure of an angle as the length of the arc on the unit circle subtended by the angle.

domain: Functions: Trigonometric Functions (F-TF) — Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle
skill: Extend trig functions to all real numbers via the unit circle
description: Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise around the unit circle.

domain: Functions: Trigonometric Functions (F-TF) — Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle
skill: Graph all six basic trigonometric functions
description: Graph all 6 basic trigonometric functions. CA

domain: Functions: Trigonometric Functions (F-TF) — Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions
skill: Choose trig functions to model periodic phenomena
description: Choose trigonometric functions to model periodic phenomena with specified amplitude, frequency, and midline.

domain: Geometry: Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry (G-SRT) — Apply trigonometry to general triangles
skill: Derive the triangle area formula using sine
description: (+) Derive the formula A = 1/2 ab sin(C) for the area of a triangle by drawing an auxiliary line from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side.

domain: Geometry: Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry (G-SRT) — Apply trigonometry to general triangles
skill: Prove and use the Laws of Sines and Cosines
description: (+) Prove the Laws of Sines and Cosines and use them to solve problems.

domain: Geometry: Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry (G-SRT) — Apply trigonometry to general triangles
skill: Apply Law of Sines/Cosines to find unknown measurements
description: (+) Understand and apply the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines to find unknown measurements in right and non-right triangles (e.g., surveying problems, resultant forces).

domain: Geometry: Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations (G-GPE) [In Mathematics III, this standard addresses only circles and parabolas] — Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section
skill: Identify and graph conic sections from a general quadratic equation
description: Given a quadratic equation of the form ax² + by² + cx + dy + e = 0, use the method for completing the square to put the equation into standard form; identify whether the graph of the equation is a circle, ellipse, parabola, or hyperbola and graph the equation. CA

domain: Geometry: Geometric Measurement and Dimension (G-GMD) — Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional objects
skill: Identify 2D cross-sections and 3D rotational objects
description: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

domain: Geometry: Modeling with Geometry (G-MG) — Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations
skill: Use geometric shapes and measures to describe objects
description: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g., modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).

domain: Geometry: Modeling with Geometry (G-MG) — Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations
skill: Apply density concepts in modeling situations
description: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g., persons per square mile, BTUs per cubic foot).

domain: Geometry: Modeling with Geometry (G-MG) — Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations
skill: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems
description: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems based on ratios).

domain: Statistics and Probability: Interpreting Categorical and Quantitative Data (S-ID) — Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable
skill: Fit data to a normal distribution and estimate percentages
description: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal curve.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Making Inferences and Justifying Conclusions (S-IC) — Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments
skill: Understand statistics as inference about population parameters
description: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters based on a random sample from that population.

skill: Decide if a model is consistent with a data-generating process
description: Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating process, e.g., using simulation. For example, a model says a spinning coin falls heads up with probability 0.5. Would a result of 5 tails in a row cause you to question the model?

domain: Statistics and Probability: Making Inferences and Justifying Conclusions (S-IC) — Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies
skill: Recognize purposes of surveys, experiments, observational studies
description: Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Making Inferences and Justifying Conclusions (S-IC) — Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies
skill: Estimate population mean/proportion and margin of error
description: Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error through the use of simulation models for random sampling.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Making Inferences and Justifying Conclusions (S-IC) — Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies
skill: Compare two treatments using randomized experiment data
description: Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to decide if differences between parameters are significant.

domain: Statistics and Probability: Making Inferences and Justifying Conclusions (S-IC) — Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies
skill: Evaluate reports based on data
description: Evaluate reports based on data.
